sources.puffs: TUNING GUESS: seeded gust puffs on a space-time lattice in a frame drifting at drift x mean wind; one puff per (cell, slot) with this probability; ellipse elongated along the wind, (1 - d^2)^3 falloff; envelope rises over riseFraction of its life and fades over the rest; strength = min + (max - min) u^3 (mostly moderate, occasionally strong); overlaps combine as cap (1 - prod(1 - c_i / cap)); veer uniform in +/- veerDeg. Speed factor is 1 + excess, never a lull.
sources.steadyZone: TUNING GUESS: gusts and slow shifts fade to zero inside innerM of the Westcove basin (berths, spawn grid, H1/H2) and are at full strength beyond outerM (buoy S at 665 m), smoothstep in between, so the tutorial sails in a steady north wind.
sources.shifts: TUNING GUESS: slow time-only oscillation of the wind direction, a sum of two sine waves (5 deg / 280 s and 3 deg / 97 s) with seeded phases, scaled by the shift strength. Position independent.
sources.visual: VISUAL ESTIMATE, render only: the sim speed factor sampled into a 160 x 160 world-anchored texture of 12.5 m cells (2 km across, centred on the boat), byte = 255 (factor - 1) / referenceExcess (stronger excess saturates). The shader sharpens the soft puff falloff into a patch with a rim: smoothstep(edgeLow, edgeHigh) of the map value (about +2% / +6% wind), with stronger gusts kept a little stronger; noise drifting with the puffs frays the patch edges. Patches show fully to fadeStartM from the boat and fade out by fadeEndM. A patch is not painted: it is rougher, as wind ruffles water. The sea's own slopes grow by up to waveRough, and eight fine ripples (15-62 cm, within 45 deg of the mean downwind direction, RMS slope rippleSlope at full gust, at their real speed) appear (src/render/gustMap.ts). Ripples fade into unresolved roughness well before they get near pixel size: it broadens the sun glint (a wider, energy-conserving glitter toward the sun), lowers the sky reflection by fresnelDrop x that slope variance, and lifts the reflected sky direction by skyLift x the RMS slope, since the facets facing a low eye mirror higher, darker sky than the bright horizon: that is what makes a cat's paw read as a dark patch from the side. Mean-square slope of wind ripples is of order 0.01-0.03 at light winds (Cox and Munk 1954, from memory, not checked against the paper), which rippleSlope 0.12 sits in.
